papers.title: Recipe card
lines: Yorkshire pudding: equal cups of flour, egg and milk. Hot fat. Do not open the oven.
Written underneath in a firmer hand: 'DO NOT OPEN THE OVEN.'

papers.title: Last shift note
lines: Sixty-one years down, man and boy. Left my lamp on the hook, as a courtesy.
Whoever has it next, keep it lit. Yours, a proud Barnsley lad, forty-seven pounds heavier than at the start.

trail.clue: The old lamp man hid his spare behind the big rock. Go and look.

papers.title: Third-class ticket
lines: York to Scarborough, return, for a day by the sea.
Underneath, in a child's writing: 'It was cold. I had the best chips of my life.'

papers.title: Fisherman's letter
lines: Dear Mary, we shall be in on the tide, God and the engine willing.
Put the kettle on at four. Put another on at five in case I am slow.
If I am very slow, send the dog.

papers.title: Hand-drawn map
lines: A rough sketch of the moor: 'Stone with a hole in it.' 'The wet bit.' 'Where Colin fell in.' 'Pub, hopefully.'
An X marks a spot the author says is 'a surprise'. The ink has run in the rain.

trail.clue: Someone wrote 'a surprise' at an X near the lamp post. It seems worth digging.

papers.title: Maker's mark card
lines: Every knife from this works has a stamp: a crowned S and my initials.
Bad knives get 'MADE IN SHEFFIELD' crossed out and sent to Rotherham.

papers.title: Meadow notice
lines: The hay is not to be cut before the orchids have seeded. Signed, Miss Thwaite, and the orchids.
Anyone who disagrees can take it up with her in person at the gate, at a time of her choosing.
